# Native mode: operators and edits

Thirteen built-in operators plus public registered Python functions. Positional arguments are graph inputs; settings are keywords. Every operator returns one table.

## Edit statements

A call has `python` and `statements` strings; an unused string is empty. Both cannot be empty.

```text
set records: scan(files='data/example.csv')
set summary: aggregate(records, outputs={'rows': count()})
```

A set replaces the complete definition, inputs, settings, and explicit doc override. Consumers remain connected to its ID. Use `delete id` to remove an existing node. Write each ID once; resolve references against the final acyclic graph. Delete or rewire consumers in the same call as their deleted input. All built-ins accept doc metadata.

## Built-in contracts

```text
scan(files=..., format="auto", skip_lines=0, header=True, names=None, all_text=False, delim=None, comment=None, widths=None, sheet=None, encoding=None, file_column=None, preview=None)
    Read local files/globs or lists: CSV/TSV, text, Excel, HTML tables, tabular JSON/JSONL, or Parquet. names requires header=False; all_text preserves codes; sheet selects a sheet/table. preview is an integer 1..200 for raw layout/metadata, not ordinary result samples. format: auto, csv, lines, fwf, whitespace, excel, html, json, parquet. TSV uses auto or csv with delim="\t". Multiple sources are deduplicated, sorted by resolved path, and column-aligned. header=True takes column names from the first retained row; names supplies one name per column and requires header=False. skip_lines is a nonnegative count of initial physical lines/rows to skip. delim is one character or "whitespace"; omission sniffs comma, tab, semicolon, or pipe. widths is a list of positive field widths for fwf. encoding is a text codec name. sheet is an Excel sheet name or zero-based index, or an HTML table zero-based index; full reads default to the first sheet/table. file_column names a new provenance column containing each source basename. Optional None settings equal omission. preview=1..200 returns raw layout; Parquet and recognized binary/compressed files return metadata only. Full Parquet is supported; specialized binary/compressed sources need custom loaders. comment is a one-character reader setting, not documentation: delimited/whitespace and inferred-width readers ignore text from the marker onward; explicit-width fwf skips lines beginning with it after whitespace. Raw lines/previews preserve source text. Format-specific settings: csv/whitespace allow header,names,skip_lines,encoding,delim,comment; fwf substitutes widths for delim; lines allows skip_lines,encoding and yields line_no and line (header=False and names=["line"] restate that and are accepted); excel allows header,names,skip_lines,sheet; html additionally allows encoding; json allows encoding; parquet has no additional reader settings. preview also accepts skip_lines except for binary/Parquet metadata. Inapplicable settings fail. JSON accepts records, one object, or column arrays; nested dictionaries flatten to dotted names.

project(t, keep=None, drop=None, rename=None)
    Keep or drop columns, then rename them with {old: new}. Row order and count stay unchanged. Provide at least one of keep, drop, or rename; keep and drop are mutually exclusive. keep preserves the requested column order. Missing columns and name collisions fail.

cast(t, columns={"column": dtype}, errors="raise")
    Convert named columns to str, int64, float64, bool, or datetime(format=..., tz=...). Failed conversions raise, or become null with errors="null"; naive timestamps require a timezone. Normalize text in a custom function before casting. columns is a nonempty mapping from column names to unquoted dtype descriptors, including names such as doc or errors. datetime(format="%Y-%m-%d", tz="UTC") accepts an explicit format and timezone.

filter(t, lambda row: condition)
    Keep the rows for which the condition over a read-only row mapping returns True; False or null drops. A registered predicate with settings also works: filter(t, predicate="name", settings={...}). Preserves columns and order; measures kept/rejected/null counts and bounded rejected-value frequencies. Example: set adults: filter(people, lambda row: row["age"] is not None and row["age"] >= 21). The lambda can call registered functions. A condition reused with different values can be registered instead: def keep(row, *, minimum=18): return row["age"] is not None and row["age"] >= minimum, then set adults: filter(people, predicate="keep", settings={"minimum": 21}). Only bool or a scalar missing value is accepted; numbers, strings, arrays, and Series fail. Missing input values appear as None. Functions share authored definitions; one fresh namespace per operator invocation is shared across its rows. The predicate cannot mutate the row mapping. Rejected includes null verdicts. When profiles are collected, frequencies describe source values among all rejected rows for up to eight actually-read columns, with three first-encountered values each and an other count; they are not top frequencies or causal explanations. Updating a definition the condition uses invalidates this filter and its descendants.

map(t, lambda row: {**row, "new": value})
    Turn each row into a new row: the dict the lambda returns is that row of the output. {**row, ...} keeps the input columns; returning only some keys keeps only those. One row out per row in, in order. Example: set priced: map(orders, lambda row: {**row, "unit_price": None if row["quantity"] in (None, 0) else row["amount"] / row["quantity"]}). Every row must return the same keys; values are scalars or None, and each column's type is inferred from them (ints and floats mix to float64; datetimes need a timezone). Missing input values appear as None. The lambda can call registered functions; logic across rows (grouping, differences between rows) belongs in aggregate, window, or a registered table function. The columns the lambda reads are measured, and the tool result lists added and dropped columns.

aggregate(t, by=[], outputs={"output": reducer(...)})
    One row per group; by=[] gives one overall row. outputs maps names to reducers. count() counts rows, count(column) non-null values; reductions skip nulls except first, all-null sum is null, stddev is sample standard deviation. Reducers: count(), count(column), count_distinct(column), sum(column), mean(column), min(column), max(column), median(column), stddev(column), first(column). count_distinct excludes nulls; null group keys form a group. Output names must not duplicate group keys. Numeric reducers require numeric columns.

join(left, right, on=None, how="inner", nulls_equal=False, suffix="_right", validate="many_to_many")
    on is a column, list of columns, or [(left_col, right_col)]. how: inner, left, right, full, cross, semi, anti. semi keeps the left rows with a match, anti those without, each once, left columns only. For a cross join, omit on or use None/[]; join(how="cross") attaches a single-row benchmark to every input row. Null keys do not match by default. validate: many_to_many, one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one; cross uses many_to_many. A colliding right column gets suffix, repeated until free (the tool result lists renames); output order is unspecified.

union(first, second, ..., schema="strict")
    Stack tables in input order, retaining duplicates. strict requires matching schemas; align fills absent columns with null. Cast incompatible types first. schema="strict" requires matching column names and types; schema="align" uses first-seen column order and fills absent cells with null. Incompatible types still require explicit conversion.

distinct(t, columns=None, keep="first")
    Keep one whole row per key (all columns by default). keep="first" or "last"; missing keys compare equal. Preserves relative row order.

sort(t, by=[...], nulls="last")
    Stable sort: by=["amount"] ascending, or by=[("amount", "desc"), "name"]. nulls="first" or "last".

limit(t, n=..., offset=0)
    Keep n rows from offset. Sort first when selecting a top-k. n must be an integer >= 1 and offset an integer >= 0. An offset past the end returns an empty table with the same schema.

window(t, partition_by=[], order_by=[...], outputs={"output": window_spec(...)})
    Add named outputs using lag, lead, row_number, rank, or dense_rank within ordered partitions; ranks start at 1 and output retains input row order. lag(column, offset=1), lead(column, offset=1), row_number(), rank(), dense_rank(). Null partition keys share a partition; null order values sort last. Add tie-break keys when required.

unpivot(t, columns=[...], name="variable", value="value")
    Wide to long: one output row per input row and selected column, including nulls. Remaining columns are keys; selected columns need compatible types.

pivot(t, index=[...], columns="...", values="...")
    Long to wide. Each (index, columns) pair must be unique; aggregate first if needed. Absent cells become null, null pivot keys fail. Retrieve the result to learn its new column names.
```

## Registered Python

Public synchronous functions become operator types. A function accepts one DataFrame per ordered input edge and keyword settings, and returns one DataFrame. Zero-input functions load custom data. Imports, helpers, constants, classes, and functions accumulate as ordered definition cells. Each invocation reconstructs its own namespace; execution mutations never become session definitions. Normal Python default binding follows cell order.

```python
import pandas as pd

def adjust(table, *, factor=1):
    """Scale the numeric value column."""
    return table.assign(value=table['value'] * factor)
```

```text
set doubled: adjust(records, factor=2)
```

The receipt confirms function registration or replacement. Replacing a definition conservatively invalidates custom users, measured filters, and their descendants; execution recomputes them. Filter is a built-in measured operator using a registered predicate.
